decision: Organization of Care › 7.3 · outpatient vs inpatient · CHW · appetite test › Outpatient (community-based) management

fragment: In-depth assessment first — a medical problem needing investigation, a condition with nutritional associations, a feeding concern, or anthropometry: WAZ < −2 SD, WLZ < −2 SD, or MUAC < 110 mm (from 6 weeks to under 6 months). decision: Step 1 · Hypoglycaemia › 7.4.1 · 10% glucose 50 ml · feed every 2 h › Diagnosis
fragment: Measure blood glucose immediately if it can be done quickly (e.g. Dextrostix). Hypoglycaemia = blood glucose < 3 mmol/L (< 54 mg/dl). (The SugarFACT trial found that raising the treatment threshold did not reduce mortality, so the standard cut-off stands.)

decision: Step 2 · Hypothermia › 7.4.2 · re-warm · feed · treat infection › Monitoring & prevention
fragment: Take the rectal temperature every 2 h until it rises > 36.5 °C (every 30 min if a heater is used). Keep the child covered at all times, especially at night; keep the head covered.

decision: Step 8 · Catch-up Growth Feeding › 7.4.8 · F-100 / RUTF · avoid heart failure › Discharge from nutritional treatment
fragment: Discharge requires BOTH anthropometric criteria — WHZ ≥ −2 AND MUAC ≥ 125 mm — with no oedema for at least 2 weeks ([§7.6.2](topic:who-imci-7-6-2-discharge-criteria)). fragment: For a child 2–5 years (measured standing), find the row for the child's height, then read the weight across the −3 SD … 3 SD columns. −3 SD = severe acute malnutrition (SAM); −2 to −3 SD = moderate wasting.
